decisions.reason: The air quality sensor module is a Bricklet built on the firm's core sensor, firmware and API-generation expertise, so in-house R&D lets it interpret early results and refine it.
As the third generation of an established analog measurement module, it builds directly on accumulated knowledge and fits the firm's iterative hardware-generation strategy.

The MQTT proxy extends the firm's software bindings and communication stack, which is close to its in-house API and firmware competence, and it adds value across the whole platform at low maintenance cost.
The CAN bus interface fits the firm's existing connectivity modules and electronics know-how, serving its automation and robotics customers with a related technology.
The CO2 sensor module follows the proven Bricklet sensor pattern, so the firm can readily assimilate feedback and improve it within its modular architecture.

The touch panel accessory lies somewhat further from the core sensing and control knowledge, but it complements the existing display and HMI modules and remains within the firm's electronics capability.
